search-summary-2021.note: Relayed through a search summary. Pages not read.

claims.claim: The season was cool and dry. Cold weather delayed bud break.
claims.note: One source. It gives roughly 5 to 6 inches of rain from late 2020 through spring, and another version of the interview says 20 to 21 inches. See conflicts.

claims.claim: Summer was mild, with cool mornings and plenty of fog. There was little or no heat, and no Labor Day heat wave.
Harvest ran in line with or a bit behind the historical average. Long hang time let fruit ripen fully.
Yields were at or just below the historical average.
claims.note: Search summaries say Pinot Noir yields fell sharply except in Sta. Rita Hills, where they were above average. Not confirmed on a page.

claims.claim: Wines show great depth of flavor, lower potential alcohol and high acidity. Cabernet Sauvignon and Pinot Noir stood out in the state report. SAMsARA singles out a complex Chardonnay.
claims.note: Producer and trade-group statements. No independent critic page read.

claims.claim: Tyler Thomas of Dierberg called ripening weather 'about as ideal as you could ask for in Santa Barbara County'.
claims.quote: about as ideal as you could ask for in Santa Barbara County

claims.claim: Mildew pressure hit some vineyards, and the Alisal Fire was a threat late in the season.
claims.note: One source. No smoke effects reported.

claims.claim: A Vinous assessment is reported as mixed for Santa Barbara Pinot Noir in 2021.
claims.note: Second hand. The Vinous page was not read.

conflicts: Rainfall: SAMsARA's page gives about 5 to 6 inches, and another version of the interview gives 20 to 21 inches for the rainy season.
Pinot Noir yields: the two read pages say at or just below average. Search summaries say sharp drops outside Sta. Rita Hills.
gaps: No frost or flowering detail found for 2021.
No exact harvest dates and no tonnage figures.
Nothing split between Santa Maria Valley and Sta. Rita Hills. Sources speak for the county.
No independent critic vintage page read. Vinous 2021 article text did not load.
Filed under central-coast but the sources cover Santa Barbara County only.

sheet.vintage: A cool, dry year in Santa Barbara County. Summer was mild and foggy, with no big heat. Harvest ran on the late side, and the whites kept bright acidity.
